note: The British Columbia Trade Development Corporation (BC Trade), added 2026-11-13 with its logo (research/identity/bc-trade-vector-2026-11-13). Its life cycle follows BC Systems Corporation's pattern: operations passed elsewhere in 1996, legal dissolution years later.

records.name: British Columbia Trade Development Corporation
records.description: Crown corporation established in 1989 under the Trade Development Corporation Act to help British Columbia businesses develop export markets: advice and technical assistance, market research and overseas business contacts, grants, loans and loan guarantees, investment in export enterprises, and the administration of government export programs. The Act allowed it to be called “B.C. Trade”. Announced in July 1988 as part of an international business development strategy. In March 1996 its functions were combined with those of the British Columbia Investment Office and the ministry’s Industry and Investment Division as the British Columbia Trade and Investment Office (BCTIO), in the Ministry of Employment and Investment. The corporation was then wound up — settling loan guarantees and disposing of investments — and dissolved on 21 November 2003, when its Act was repealed.
records.establishedMeaning: the Trade Development Corporation Act received Royal Assent on 1 June 1989, the date BC Trade’s own launch advertisement gives for the new export organization’s arrival
records.endedMeaning: dissolved when its enabling Act was repealed on 21 November 2003 (B.C. Reg. 418/2003; the order in council was approved the day before), its remaining assets, rights, obligations and liabilities passing to the Province; it had stopped operating in March 1996

operationalEnd.meaning: its functions combined with those of the British Columbia Investment Office and the Industry and Investment Division to form the British Columbia Trade and Investment Office, within the Ministry of Employment and Investment
